title: A run for everyone
text: In 2004, thirteen runners timed themselves over five kilometres in a London park, using stopwatches and a spreadsheet emailed afterwards. The idea — a free, weekly, timed run, open to anyone — {{1}} into parkrun, an organisation that now {{2}} millions of registered runners at thousands of locations on five continents. Nothing about it is {{3}}: no prizes, no entries, no minimum speed, and the results page {{4}} everyone from international athletes to walkers who take an hour. The {{5}} explains itself: what keeps people running is not medals but the promise of a friendly crowd, a number to try to beat, and coffee afterwards. Public health researchers {{6}} the attention: regular, gentle, sociable exercise is exactly what doctors {{7}}, and the run functions as a habit machine — the same time, the same place, every week, with a community that notices your {{8}}. Cities have started treating it as infrastructure: family doctors in some areas prescribe attendance, and councils compete for new courses. What began as thirteen people and a spreadsheet is now, arguably, the largest running event in the world — held every Saturday, rain or shine, and free for ever.

gaps.explanation: 'the idea developed into parkrun' — grew and expanded into it; debunk = expose a myth, dwindle = shrink.
'now boasts millions of registered runners' — has and is proud of it; broom = sweep.
'nothing about it is exclusive' — restricted to a privileged few; exhaustive = complete, exquisite = beautifully made.
'the results page features everyone' — displays them prominently; fixture = a fixed sports match.
'the formula explains itself' — the recipe that produces the result; formality = something done for show.
'researchers welcome the attention' — are glad of it; weld = join metal, whittle = carve away gradually.
'exactly what doctors prescribe' — recommend as treatment; proscribe = ban, a classic confusable.
'a community that notices your absence' — the fact that you are missing; obscurity = the state of being unknown.
